chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from one of our companions, from Abu

Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever satiates a believer, Paradise becomes obligatory for him; and whoever satiates a disbeliever, it becomes a right upon Allah to fill his belly with As-Saqar (Hellfire), whether he was a believer or a disbeliever.'

key_terms.أَشْبَعَ: to satiate or feed until full

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of feeding a believer versus a disbeliever according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this hadith to underscore the transformative power of charity, where the spiritual state of the recipient dictates the divine outcome. While feeding a believer secures their entry into Paradise, feeding a disbeliever triggers a specific divine retribution where their belly is filled with Zaqum, illustrating that the act itself carries karmic weight based on the recipient's faith. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the intrinsic value of the believer's presence and the tangible consequences of interacting with them.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Yahya Al Wasity, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘The one who satiates a Momin, the Paradise would be Obligated for him; and the one who satiates an infidel, he would have a right upon Allahazwj that Heazwj Fills his inside with ‘Al-Zaqoum’ (a bitter fruit of Hell), whether he was a Momin or an Infidel’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from abu Yahya al-Wasiti from certain individuals of our people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Paradise becomes necessary for one who satisfies the hunger of a believer. For one who satisfies the hunger of an unbeliever (for his disbelief) it becomes necessary for Allah to fill his belly with al-Zaqum, the fruit of hell, regardless of his being a believer or unbeliever.”
